Known differences between internal/markdown (goldmark) and Commonmarker (comrak)
================================================================================
Every golden pair in this directory (the original corpus and the extra-*.md pairs) matches
exactly outside <pre> blocks, so the knownDifferences map in internal/markdown/golden_test.go
is empty. The items below were found by differential testing against real Commonmarker
(about 18,000 generated samples plus the 87 real documents) and are NOT covered by any golden.
They are rare, structural corner cases; none occurs in the real corpus.

1. Syntax highlighting is not byte-identical (by design)
   Commonmarker colours code with syntect, the Go renderer with chroma. The <pre style=...>,
   <code class="language-x"> wrappers, the escaped text and the one-<span>-per-token shape match;
   the token boundaries and some colours differ. The test helper strips <span> tags inside
   <pre>...</pre> on both sides before comparing. Unknown or missing languages render exactly
   like syntect's plain text (one span per line).
   Additionally each document gets a highlight budget of 32 KB of fenced code; blocks past it
   are plain text (same wrapper). Chroma costs ~1.5 ms/KB, so without the budget the 200 KB
   git-sync golden took ~170 ms; with it, ~40 ms.

2. A single quote pairing across a partially overlapping emphasis
   `'a *b' c*`   comrak: ‘a <em>b’ c</em>     Go: ’a <em>b’ c</em>
   cmark pairs ' and " on one delimiter stack shared with emphasis; Go pairs them among the
   siblings of one inline container. Only a quote pair that straddles an emphasis boundary
   (opener outside, closer inside, emphasis not closed before the quote) differs, and only in
   the glyph of the opening quote. Properly nested or separate pairs match.

3. Link reference definition immediately followed by a block that cmark treats as text
   `[r]: /u` directly followed by an empty bullet line `- `, or by `---`, or by a lazy
   continuation `1. a`/`   b` item. goldmark resolves reference definitions when the
   paragraph closes, after the next line already interrupted it; cmark resolves them first.
   Example: "[r]: /u\n---" comrak <p>—</p>, Go <hr />. Two-block definitions followed by a blank
   line (the normal way to write them) match.

4. Empty bullet followed by an indented nested list on the next line
   "*\n  - nested"   comrak: one item containing the nested list; Go: an empty item, then the
   nested list as a sibling. (A bullet that has text on its first line is unaffected.)

5. Invalid UTF-8 is an error, as in Rails
   Commonmarker raises EncodingError for input that is not valid UTF-8; Render returns
   ErrInvalidUTF8 and the caller decides how to degrade. NUL bytes become U+FFFD, a leading BOM
   is dropped, CRLF and lone CR become LF, all exactly like comrak.

Behaviours reproduced on purpose (so they are not differences): smart punctuation incl. dash runs
("-----" becomes em+en), quote flanking rules, comrak's inline-time www/scheme autolinks on the
raw source (never inside an open "["), post-parse email autolinks incl. mailto:/xmpp: prefixes and
bracket depth, href escaping (&#x27;, %-encoding, &amp;), anchor ids incl. duplicates and Rust-style
lowercasing, type 7 HTML blocks that start on lazy continuation lines and may end in a tab.
